anomalies.observed: J8 is a 2-pin screw terminal on the MCU sheet. Its pin 2 sits on /Microcontroller/NET0014, the GPIO1 heater-control net that also drives U7 IN/DIAG_EN and the D9 indicator LED anode. Pin 1 is on GND. No +12V pin appears on J8.
anomalies.expected: The specification places 12 V fan-header pins on J7/J8 pin 2 ("the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)"). In this build the 12 V fan-header pins are J4.2 and J13.2 on +12V, and J8.2 is instead routed to the heater GPIO control net.

evidence.quote: the two fan-header 12 V pins (`J7`/`J8` pin 2)

anomalies.impact: If J8 is meant to be a 12 V fan or accessory connector, its 12 V pin is actually a GPIO1 heater-control signal, so an external device would be driven by or would load the control line instead of receiving 12 V. This is uncertain because the reference numbering differs from the specification in several places.

parsed.summary: The passives, power rails, SPI bus and chip-select wiring are consistent with the specification and with sound practice. The only notable deviation is that J8 pin 2, which the specification describes as a 12 V fan-header pin, is on the GPIO1 heater-control net, though reference numbering differs enough that this is low confidence.
